A patient presents with the following case:


A 32-year-old woman presents with new-onset focal seizures involving the right hand. MRI reveals a 3.8 cm non-enhancing, T2-hyperintense lesion in the left frontal lobe without mass effect or midline shift. She undergoes gross total resection with clean surgical margins confirmed on postoperative imaging. Histopathology reveals a WHO grade 2 astrocytoma with IDH1 R132H mutation confirmed by immunohistochemistry. ATRX expression is lost, and 1p/19q codeletion is absent, consistent with astrocytoma. Her KPS is 95, and she has no residual neurological deficits. Given her age under 40 and the extent of resection achieved, she is monitored with serial imaging. She remains clinically stable for three years on surveillance MRI scans. At her 38-month follow-up, MRI demonstrates interval increase in the T2/FLAIR signal abnormality at the resection margin, measuring 1.6 cm, consistent with tumor recurrence. She remains neurologically intact with well-controlled seizures on levetiracetam.
